subject: Caching economics — post-demo numbers & next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Liu <jared@finplus.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Caching economics — post-demo numbers & next steps

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can lock down pricing math for the PO/PR side.

Recap from today
- Expected monthly activity: you mentioned ~3M conversational requests (prompt + completion pairs), with an average total token consumption of ~900 tokens/request (300 prompt + 600 completion).
- Goal budget band: the finance sponsor is looking for an effective cost of roughly $180–$250 per 1M tokens (we took note of that as a target).
- Primary workload characteristics: ~40% of requests are form/template-driven (high repetition of opening prompt chunks), rest are freeform.

Assumptions I used for the pricing worksheet attached:
- Raw serving cost (baseline model vHot-1): $350 per 1M tokens (this is the compute+ops unit we expect without caching).
- Prefix cache strategy: cache first N tokens of prompts for known templates; conservative hit-rate assumption = 55%.
- Effective cost math at 55% prefix hit: effective $/1M tokens = baseline * (1 - hit_rate) = $350 * 0.45 = $157.5 per 1M tokens.
- If we increase hit to 70% (aggressive templating), effective cost drops to $105 per 1M tokens.

Ask / next steps
1) Can you confirm the 3M requests/mo and the ~900 token average? If those shift ±20% it materially changes the unit economics.
2) Do you have a list of the top 10 templates or the common prompt starters we can review? We can run a quick prefix clustering analysis and estimate a realistic hit range.
3) If the finance team wants a conservative floor to approve, would they accept our 55% hit baseline or do we need to price at a 40% hit to be safe?

I'm attaching a one-page worksheet (pricing-model-v2.xlsx) showing the calc and two scenarios. If you confirm volumes and share the templates, we can produce a short appendix mapping those templates to estimated hit rates and send a firm quote.

Thanks — Diego

Diego — thanks for the follow-up and the clear worksheet. A few quick confirmations from our side:
- Volume: current expectation is ~3.2M requests/month, but that could grow to 4–5M in Q4 if the pilot metrics look good.
- Tokens: average closer to 1,000 tokens/request when you include metadata + longer completions; the 900 number is a reasonable mid-case.
- Templates: we have ~8 stable templates that cover onboarding flows and several help responses (I can export them). We expect template-backed traffic to be about 45–50% initially; we can probably push that to 60–65% if we hard-enforce the template usage in the UI.

On price target: finance prefers conservatism. They will likely sign-off if we can show an effective cost <= $220/1M under a conservative 50% hit assumption. Anything above that will require additional approvals.

Diego — quick technical read and recommended conservative assumptions: 

1) Baseline mapping
- The $350/1M baseline is within range for vHot-1 for the token mix described. Use $350 as our public baseline but call it "baseline compute+infra" in the quote.

2) Prefix cache expectations (top-8 templates)
- Conservative (what we should price to): 50% hit. This assumes templates have modest variation (user name, id) and we match on normalized prefixes.
- Achievable with minimal engineering effort: 60% hit. Requires basic normalization (strip user-specific tokens, canonicalize timestamps, lowercasing) + a short prefix length (first 40–80 tokens).
- Aggressive/optimized: 70–75% hit. Requires templating enforcement on UI or re-write to use structured inputs; also a tuning window for cache TTLs and tokenization-aware prefix sizes.

3) Effect on effective $/1M (quick numbers)
- At 50% hit => effective = $350 * (1 - 0.50) = $175/1M
- At 60% hit => effective = $350 * 0.40 = $140/1M
- At 70% hit => effective = $350 * 0.30 = $105/1M

4) Low-friction levers to propose in the proposal
- Offer a small behavioral change: require use of one of the 8 templates for onboarding flows (can be A/B tested).
- Provide a small pre-processing SDK that canonicalizes prompts (we can ship a JS snippet).
- Include a 30-day cache telemetry window in the pilot so we can measure real hit rates and update the quote after the pilot.

5) Attachments: I exported a short heuristic doc and a pricing sheet with scenario math (pricing-model-v2.xlsx, prefix-heuristics.pdf).

Recommend we present two numbers to finance:
- Conservative quote (50% hit): effective $175/1M — this meets their <= $220/1M bar comfortably.
- Aggressive/negotiation anchor (60% hit): $140/1M with an explicit pilot clause to rebase once telemetry is available.

If Diego wants, I can draft the one-pager to send to FinPlus with those two lanes and the pilot clause.
